answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a challenge-bound sequence of modular squarings, with every step depending on the previous one. A GPU cannot shorten that identity’s chain by parallelizing its squarings; clones may run separate chains concurrently, but each still incurs the full sequential delay and computation. A verifier checks the result with a Wesolowski proof, making the summit, ridge, and canyon of clone creation costly in elapsed time rather than merely in storage.
